messages.subject: Trouble on running the stan model
parts: I have a data set containing user id, item id and rating score. There are nearly 40,000 lines of data and I am implement pmf model on it with stan. But it takes nearly half an hour and just runs all the time, throwing no error but no result neither. My code is attached. Could you please take a look and tell me what is the problem? Thank you in advance.

messages.subject: Re: Trouble on running the stan model

I have run the code again in terminal and this time several errors occur:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be  rejected because of the following issue:
Exception thrown at line 35: stan::math::normal_log: Scale parameter is 0, but must be > 0!

Seems that it is talking about these lines of code:

for (d in 1:D){
        r[d] ~ normal(u[jj[d]] * i[ii[d]]', alpha);
    }

    for (n in 1: N){

    }
    for (m in 1:M){
        i[m] ~ normal(0, alpha_i );
    }
    for (d in 1:D_new){
        r_new[d] ~ normal(u[jj_new[d]] * i[ii_new[d]]', alpha);
    }


i wonder what is wrong in my code and how can I fix it? Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Trouble on running the stan model
parts:
The line is 35, so you should be able to figure out exactly
where there's a problem. This is one reason you want your Stan
programs in their own files.

This looks like a continuation of that last question.
You want a prior on the alpha, but if the data's consistent
with zero variance, you could have a bigger problem. You
ideally want all your data to be unit scaled, not some small
epsilon scaled.

- Bob
